title: Closed-Loop Hydrometallurgical Recycling of Lithium-Ion Batteries
promptText:
The diagram below illustrates the industrial process by which spent electric-vehicle lithium-ion batteries are recycled to manufacture new battery cells.

Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

Write at least 150 words.

chartSpec.title: Closed-Loop Hydrometallurgical Battery Recycling Process
chartSpec.subtitle: Seven-stage industrial recovery cycle from spent EV packs to cathode synthesis

steps.detail: End-of-life EV packs are tested and electrically discharged in brine tanks to prevent thermal hazards.
Robotic units remove aluminium casings, wiring harnesses, and plastic modules for separate recycling.
Cells are crushed under nitrogen atmosphere (oxygen-free) into a fine granular mixture.
Copper and steel foils are filtered out, isolating 'black mass' powder rich in critical metals.
Black mass is dissolved in warm sulphuric acid solution (60°C) to extract metal ions into liquid phase.
Battery-grade lithium, nickel, and cobalt salts (99.5% purity) are selectively crystallized.
Purified salts are synthesized into active cathode material for new EV battery cells.
